items.summary: Rescan with the fixed scan_nvidia: 12 files carry the pre-2017 CUDA samples EULA-pointer notice -- the vendored src/include/helper_*.h set AND h2o4gpu's own src/gpu/bwcheck.cu and src/include/exception.h, which copied the header. Project is awaiting-fork; the licence ruling should precede adoption. Submodule scan coverage was partial (cub pin). POLICY (2026-08-24): swap the vendored NVIDIA-EULA files for BSD-3 versions (or drop the dead ones) at the tip BEFORE any fork is created, so the proprietary versions are never hosted at our tip. All flagged files are dead in the build, so this is a pre-adoption commit, not a port blocker.

utils/surface.py has no 'in scope, not yet done' state for a component a port still owes after it claims success (stage ported or later). h2o4gpu files platform:windows under scoped_out as a labelled placeholder because of this, although jeff's ruling 3 keeps Windows in scope and the windows gate is required and unwaived. Add an owed state (or an equivalent) to surface.py check, then move h2o4gpu's platform:windows entry there.

/Ob2 device miscompile suspected on gfx1151 Windows (TheRock ROCm, clang-cl): the double-precision FuncEval reduction kernel (rocPRIM reduce over zip_function<FuncEvalF<double>>) in src/gpu/h2o4gpuglm.cu never completes with /O2 /Ob2 and completes with /Ob1. Reproducer being extracted: reduce the kernel to a standalone .hip, diff /Ob1 vs /Ob2 ISA, draft the compiler issue for jeff. Until then the port carries /Ob1 on h2o4gpuglm.cu (CMakeLists.txt, clang-cl HIP front end only); drop that property once the compiler fix lands.

Inherited upstream multi-GPU KMeans bugs (CUDA and HIP alike, present before the port): (1) kmeans_transform with n_gpus>1 returns wrong distances for every row: each GPU's chunk-by-k distance block is column-major and the blocks are concatenated, but KMeansH2O.transform reshapes the whole buffer as one column-major (rows, k) matrix (gfx942, n_gpus=2: argmin agreement 0.26-0.34 vs NumPy; each block alone matches to 3.8e-16). (2) With rows % n_gpus != 0, fit, predict and transform never process the last rows % n_gpus rows (rows/n_gpu per GPU; 'TODO: that may ignore up to n_gpu - 1 rows'): their labels are 0 and their distances 0. Single-GPU is correct. Needs a person's ruling: fix in the port (strided host copy for (1); remainder rows for (2)) or report upstream only.
